business_problem: MosaicML needed cloud infrastructure that could support growing demand for AI services and let it train large, complex generative AI models faster and at lower cost for enterprise customers.
solution_summary: MosaicML added Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) as the preferred infrastructure underneath its managed machine-learning platform so it could meet rising demand for enterprise generative AI services. In the described setup, customers bring large training datasets and model-building workloads to MosaicML, while the platform offloads cluster and hardware complexity to OCI. MosaicML uses OCI AI infrastructure and OCI Compute bare metal GPU instances to run training and inference jobs, with NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs supplying accelerator capacity. OCI Supercluster contributes ultra-low-latency networking and HPC storage so jobs can scale across very large GPU pools. The platform then helps enterprises operationalize custom models, and customers such as Twelve Labs deploy those trained multimodal models to search, classify, and otherwise use video data more effectively.

data_flow: MosaicML customers bring large training datasets and model workloads into MosaicML workflows running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Training and inference jobs execute on OCI AI infrastructure using OCI Compute bare metal GPU instances, while OCI Supercluster supplies low-latency networking and HPC storage and NVIDIA A100 GPUs provide acceleration. The resulting models are then deployed by customers such as Twelve Labs for video search, classification, and related applications.
